outcome.answer: For large-scale recommendation systems, compute requirements can be estimated with scaling-law experiments that vary model size, training data, and compute, then measure performance to find compute-efficient allocations. Kunlun studies this relationship for massive-scale recommendation models [2], while behavioral foundation-model experiments vary compute budgets and deployment-relevant choices to derive compute-optimal recipes [4]. Component-level profiling can help locate hardware bottlenecks and guide optimization [5]. For inference, measure workload costs and consider sharing request-side computation across candidates to improve efficiency [1].
